title: 4p+1 maximal climbs
words: Show the 4p + 1 prime map can climb arbitrarily high above its starting point before falling into its loop.
math: Prove $\sup_p \max_k P_4^k(p)/p=\infty$, where $P_4(p)=P(4p+1)$.

title: Periodic billiards in Gerver's sofa
words: Show a billiard ball in Gerver's sofa has a periodic path that bounces off at least five different boundary pieces.
math: Prove the billiard in Gerver's sofa has a periodic orbit meeting at least 5 of its 18 boundary arcs.

title: Few periodic points of square-plus-one
words: Count the numbers up to X that lie on a loop of the square-plus-one map. Show there are very few.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le X: Q^k(n)=n\text{ for some }k\ge1\}=X^{o(1)}$, where $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$.

title: Isoperimetric profile of the spectre
words: Among all clusters of n spectre tiles, find the smallest possible perimeter, asymptotically, with the exact constant.
math: Prove $\min\{|\partial S|:S$ a union of $n$ tiles in a spectre tiling$\}\sim c\sqrt n$ and determine $c$.

title: Seven-free Gaussian primes
words: Show infinitely many primes a² + b² have both a and b free of the digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $a^2+b^2$ with $a,b$ positive integers free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Sofa constant digits
words: Show the digits of Gerver's sofa area do not end in a repeating pattern in base 2 either, and give an explicit irrationality measure bound.
math: Prove $\mu_G$ is irrational with irrationality measure $\le 100$.

title: Minimal degree of a Jacobian counterexample
words: The 2026 counterexamples have degree 7. Find the smallest degree any 3D counterexample can have.
math: Determine $\min\{\deg F: F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ non-invertible Keller map$\}$.

title: Irrational prime weights
words: Add up 1/(p·2^p) over all primes p. Show the total is irrational.
math: Prove $\sum_{p}\frac{1}{p\,2^{p}}$ is irrational.

title: The angel on the hat
words: An angel moves up to k tiles per turn on a hat tiling; a devil deletes one tile per turn. Find the least k for which the angel escapes forever.
math: Determine the least $k$ such that the angel of power $k$ (moves to any tile within graph distance $k$) wins against the devil on every hat tiling's adjacency graph.

title: The hat is not spectral
words: Fuglede's conjecture predicts that a shape that cannot tile by translations has no orthogonal basis of exponentials. Prove this for the hat.
math: Prove there is no $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with $\{e^{2\pi i\lambda\cdot x}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ an orthogonal basis of $L^2(\text{hat})$.

title: Prime cubes with one shift
words: Show infinitely many quadruples of primes satisfy x³ + y³ = z³ + w³ + 1.
math: Prove infinitely many prime solutions $(x,y,z,w)$ of $x^3+y^3=z^3+w^3+1$.

title: Sandpile identity on hats
words: The abelian sandpile on a large hat-tiled region has an identity element that looks like a fractal picture. Show it has a scaling limit.
math: Prove the sandpile identity on hat-tiled $L$-balls, rescaled by $L$, converges weakly (as a height-density measure) and that the limit is not rotationally invariant.

title: First appearances in Prime Nim
words: The smallest pile with Grundy value k in Prime Nim grows extremely fast. Show it grows at least exponentially in k.
math: Let $a(k)=\min\{n:G(n)=k\}$ for the prime subtraction game. Prove $a(k)\ge e^{ck}$ for some $c>0$ and all $k$ for which $a(k)$ exists.

title: Square-sum edge-Hamiltonian
words: Show every edge of the square-sum graph lies on a loop through all of 1 to N, for large N.
math: Prove that for all large $N$, every edge of $S_N$ lies on a Hamiltonian cycle of $S_N$.

title: Hat Hofstadter at golden flux
words: Thread a magnetic flux through each hat tile equal to the golden ratio. Show the resulting energy spectrum is a zero-measure Cantor set.
math: For the magnetic tight-binding Hamiltonian on the hat graph with flux $\phi=(\sqrt5-1)/2$ per kite, prove $\sigma(H)$ is a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero.

title: Hat Ising critical line
words: Ising models on a hat tiling and its dual should be exactly related at their critical points. Prove the duality relation holds rigorously.
math: For the ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph $G$ and its planar dual $G^*$, prove $\sinh(2\beta_c(G))\sinh(2\beta_c(G^*))=1$.

title: Seven-free primes with prime digit sum
words: Show infinitely many primes have no digit 7 and a digit sum that is itself prime.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ free of the decimal digit 7 with $s_{10}(p)$ prime.

title: Midpoint map as a random walk
words: Show that, for a random large start, the logarithm of the midpoint-prime orbit moves like a Gaussian random walk.
math: Prove that for $n$ uniform in $[x,2x]$, the distribution of $\log m^{k}(n)-\log n$ for $k=\lfloor\log x\rfloor$ converges after normalization to a Gaussian.

title: Prime-sum Hamiltonian cycles through every edge
words: Show every edge of the prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n lies on a full prime circle.
math: Prove for all large $n$ every edge of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ lies on a Hamiltonian cycle.

title: Smooth neighbours of squares
words: Show infinitely many n have both n² − 1 and n² + 1 built only from primes below n^0.4.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $P(n^4-1)\le n^{0.4}$.

title: Potts transition on hats
words: Show the q-state Potts model on the hat tiling has a discontinuous transition for large q, and a continuous one for q = 2.
math: Prove the $q$-state Potts model on the hat graph has a first-order transition for all $q\ge q_0$ and a continuous one for $q=2$; find the least such $q_0$.

title: Bounded gaps among seven-free primes, weak
words: Show seven-free primes come in clusters: infinitely often two of them within distance x^0.9.
math: Prove $\liminf_n (q_{n+1}-q_n)/q_n^{0.9}=0$ where $(q_n)$ enumerates 7-free primes.

title: Prime-power Collatz, almost always
words: Show almost every start under the prime-power Collatz map eventually drops below its starting value.
math: For $c(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even), $(3n+1)/q(3n+1)$ ($n$ odd; $q$ = largest prime-power divisor), prove $\{n:\exists k\ c^k(n)<n\}$ has density 1.

title: Gerver sofa and the circle
words: Show the area of Gerver's sofa is not a rational combination of π and 1.
math: Prove $\mu_G\notin\mathbb{Q}+\mathbb{Q}\pi$.

title: Square-sum paths with chosen ends
words: Show you can line up 1 to N with neighbours summing to squares, starting and ending at almost any two numbers you choose.
math: Prove $S_N$ contains a Hamiltonian path whose endpoints can be prescribed arbitrarily among vertices of degree $\ge3$, for all large $N$.

title: Largest factor of the midpoint
words: For consecutive primes p < q, look at the largest prime factor of (p + q)/2. Show it exceeds p^0.5 for a positive fraction.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x: P(\tfrac{p_n+p_{n+1}}2)>p_n^{1/2}\}\gg \pi(x)$.

title: Hat Laplacian eigenvalue is transcendental
words: Show the lowest vibration frequency of a hat-shaped drum with clamped edges is transcendental.
math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ of the hat polygon (unit kite side) is transcendental.

title: An infinite square-sum line
words: Arrange the square-sum graph's vertices in an infinite line: is there an ordering of all positive integers so that neighbours always sum to a square?
math: Prove there is a bijection $\pi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\pi(i)+\pi(i+1)$ a perfect square for all $i$, in which $\pi(i)\le Ci$ for all $i$.

title: Lonely runners at Fibonacci speeds
words: Prove the lonely runner conjecture when the speeds are consecutive Fibonacci numbers.
math: Prove $\sup_t\min_{2\le i\le n+1}\|tF_i\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$ for all $n$, where $F_i$ are Fibonacci numbers.

title: Prime-power Collatz cycles
words: Show the prime-power Collatz map has no loop other than the fixed point 1.
math: Prove the only periodic orbit of $c$ is the fixed point $\{1\}$.

title: Affine prime maps all settle
words: Fix whole numbers a and b. Send a prime p to the largest prime factor of ap + b. Every case tested falls into a loop. Prove this always happens.
math: Prove that for all fixed integers $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, every orbit of $p\mapsto P(ap+b)$ on primes is eventually periodic.

title: Hyperdissipative forced blow-up
words: Fluids with extra strong viscosity never blow up above a known threshold. Show forced blow-up still happens just below it.
math: For $\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla p=-(-\Delta)^{\alpha}u+f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$, construct smooth compactly supported $f$ giving finite-time blow-up from rest for every $\alpha<5/4$.

title: Gerver sofa algebraic independence of its angles
words: Gerver's sofa is built from two special angles. Show they are algebraically independent over the rationals.
math: Prove the two transcendental switching angles $\varphi\approx0.0392$ and $\theta\approx0.6813$ in Gerver's construction are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$.

title: Polykite growth: one more digit
words: Pin the exponential growth rate of n-kite shapes to within one percent, rigorously.
math: Prove explicit bounds $a\le\lambda\le b$ with $b/a\le1.01$ for the polykite growth constant $\lambda=\lim k_n^{1/n}$.

title: Equilateral triangles of hat centres
words: Prove every hat tiling contains infinitely many equilateral triangles with tile centres as corners, at arbitrarily large scales.
math: Prove every hat tiling has tile-centre equilateral triangles of side $\ge R$ for every $R$.

title: Hard-core on the hat
words: Place particles on hat tiles with no two neighbours both occupied. Show the gas freezes into an ordered state at high density.
math: For the hard-core model on the hat graph, prove a phase transition: non-uniqueness of Gibbs measures for all activities $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$.

title: Navier–Stokes blow-up count
words: Show a single smooth forced Navier–Stokes flow can blow up at infinitely many points at once.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,T]$ such that Navier–Stokes from rest has a singular set at time $T$ of positive 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

title: Midpoint primes: odd-run lengths
words: Find the asymptotic distribution of how many odd steps in a row the midpoint-prime map takes.
math: For the midpoint-prime map $m$, prove the length of the maximal run of odd iterates starting from a uniform odd $n\le x$ converges in distribution to a geometric law, and find its parameter.

title: Long loops for affine prime maps
words: As a and b vary, the loops of p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + b get longer and longer. Prove loop lengths are unbounded.
math: Prove $\sup_{a,b}\max\{\text{length of a cycle of } p\mapsto P(ap+b)\}=\infty$.

title: Odd-cycle-free square sums
words: How many numbers up to N can you keep so the square-sum graph on them has no odd cycle?
math: Determine $\max\{|A|:A\subseteq[N],\ S_N[A]\text{ bipartite}\}/N$ asymptotically.

title: Lattice gauge on the hat
words: Show the Z/2 lattice gauge theory on a hat-tiled surface times a line has a deconfinement transition.
math: For $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory on the 3D cell complex $\mathrm{hat}\times\mathbb{Z}$, prove the Wilson loop changes from area law to perimeter law at a single critical coupling.

title: Smooth shifted primes in two bases
words: Find infinitely many primes p for which p − 1 has only small prime factors and p has no digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p$ with $P(p-1)\le p^{0.3}$.

title: Joint digit sums of primes
words: Show infinitely many primes have a prime digit sum in base 2 and in base 10 at the same time.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ have $s_2(p)$ and $s_{10}(p)$ both prime.

title: Prime-sum Hamiltonian count
words: Count the ways to arrange 1 to 2n in a circle so neighbours sum to primes. Find the growth rate.
math: Let $H_n$ count Hamiltonian cycles of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$. Prove $\log H_n=(1+o(1))\,c\,n\log n$ and find $c$.

title: RH proof, human-readable core
words: Extract from the 2026 Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis a human-readable proof under 300 pages that experts accept.
math: Produce a written proof of RH of at most 300 pages whose every step is mapped to the 2026 Lean development and which passes refereeing at a major journal.

title: Lonely runners with square speeds
words: Prove the lonely runner conjecture when all speeds are perfect squares.
math: For distinct positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_n$, prove $\sup_t\min_i\|ta_i^2\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$.

title: Lost in a hat-shaped forest
words: You are lost in a forest shaped like a hat, position and orientation unknown. Find the shortest path guaranteed to get you out.
math: Determine Bellman's escape length for the hat polygon: the least length of a curve such that every congruent placement of it inside the hat meets the boundary.

title: Star-shaped sofa
words: Find the largest sofa that turns the corner and is star-shaped: some point inside can see the whole sofa.
math: Maximize area over star-shaped sets admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor, and determine whether the optimizer is unique.

title: Chromatic number of prime-difference plus square-sum
words: Join two numbers if their sum is a square or their difference is prime. Find the colours needed for all positive integers.
math: Determine $\chi(G)$ for $G$ on $\mathbb{N}$ with $a\sim b$ iff $a+b$ is a square or $|a-b|$ is prime.

title: Hat quasicrystal Ising universality, bond-disordered
words: Randomly weaken some bonds in the hat Ising model. Show the critical behaviour still matches the clean 2D Ising class up to logs.
math: For the random-bond ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph with i.i.d. couplings in $[1,1+\varepsilon]$, prove the specific heat diverges at most as $\log\log|t|^{-1}$ near $T_c$ for small $\varepsilon$.

title: Prime-power Collatz stopping times
words: Show the prime-power Collatz map reaches 1 in about a constant times log n steps on average, and find the constant.
math: For $c=c_3$, prove $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}T_c(n)\sim\kappa\log x$ and determine $\kappa$.

title: Longest increasing run of prime gaps
words: Among the first N prime gaps, find the longest subsequence that strictly increases. Show it grows like a power of N and find the power.
math: Let $L(N)$ be the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $(p_{n+1}-p_n)_{n\le N}$. Prove $L(N)=N^{\theta+o(1)}$ and determine $\theta$.

title: Midpoint-prime, almost surely
words: Show the midpoint-prime map brings almost every start below its starting value.
math: Prove $\{n:\exists k,\ m^k(n)<n\}$ has natural density 1, without assuming any conjecture on prime gaps beyond the prime number theorem in short intervals.

title: Sidon sets of hat tiles
words: Pick hat tiles so all pairwise displacement vectors are distinct. How many can fit in a region of n tiles?
math: Determine the asymptotics of the maximum size of $A\subseteq B_L$ (hat-tiled $L$-ball, tile centres) with all differences $a-a'$, $a\ne a'$, distinct.

title: Two digit sums, independently
words: For primes, the base-2 digit sum modulo 3 and the base-10 digit sum modulo 3 should behave independently. Prove it.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: s_2(p)\equiv a,\ s_{10}(p)\equiv b \pmod 3\}\sim\tfrac19\pi(x)$ for all $a,b$.

title: Rotor walks on the spectre
words: A rotor walk on the spectre tiling should stay within bounded distance of a random walk's expected behaviour. Prove the discrepancy is bounded.
math: For rotor-router aggregation on the spectre graph with $n$ particles, prove the cluster differs from a disc of area $n$ by $O(\log n)$ in Hausdorff distance.

title: Heesch-one polykites are typical
words: Show the polykites that can be surrounded exactly once grow in number at the same exponential rate as all polykites.
math: Let $k_n^{(1)}$ count $n$-kite polykites with Heesch number exactly 1. Prove $\lim (k_n^{(1)})^{1/n}=\lim k_n^{1/n}$.

title: Boundary entropy of hat discs
words: Count the ways to tile a disc of radius R with hats, allowing tiles to stick out of the boundary. Show the count grows exponentially in R and find the rate.
math: Let $T(R)$ count hat-tile patches covering the disc of radius $R$ (each tile meeting the disc), up to translation. Prove $\log T(R)\sim\sigma R$ and compute $\sigma$.

title: Graceful forests from caterpillar seeds
words: Show forests made of large caterpillars plus one arbitrary tree are graceful-forest labelable.
math: Prove every forest $T\cup C_1\cup\dots\cup C_k$ with $T$ any tree and $C_i$ caterpillars each of size $\ge|T|$ admits a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+k\}$ with distinct edge differences.

title: Spectre electrical resistance
words: Find the exact asymptotic electrical resistance between two far-apart spectre tiles, with unit resistors on edges.
math: Prove $R(o,x)=\kappa\log|x|+O(1)$ on spectre tilings and compute $\kappa$ in closed form.

title: Midpoint-prime orbit lengths
words: Find the average number of steps the midpoint-prime map takes to reach 1, on a logarithmic scale.
math: For the midpoint-prime map $m$, prove $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}\frac{T_m(n)}{\log n}\to c$ and compute $c$, where $T_m(n)=\min\{k:m^k(n)=1\}$.

title: Weyl remainder for the hat drum
words: Count the vibration frequencies of a hat-shaped drum below a threshold. Find the true size of the error after the two leading terms.
math: For the Dirichlet Laplacian on the hat polygon, prove $N(\lambda)=\frac{|\Omega|}{4\pi}\lambda-\frac{|\partial\Omega|}{4\pi}\sqrt\lambda+O(\lambda^{\theta})$ and determine the optimal $\theta$.

title: Internal DLA on hats
words: Release walkers one at a time from a hat tile; each stops at the first unoccupied tile. Show the occupied cluster becomes a round disc.
math: For internal DLA on the hat adjacency graph with $n$ particles, prove the cluster rescaled by $\sqrt n$ converges to a Euclidean disc (with tile centres as positions).

title: Sofa as a billiard table
words: Show billiards inside Gerver's sofa is not ergodic.
math: Prove the billiard flow in Gerver's sofa has an invariant set of positive, non-full Liouville measure.

title: Seven-free square-sum chains
words: Take only the numbers up to N with no digit 7. Show they can be lined up so neighbours always sum to perfect squares, for large N.
math: Let $A_N=\{n\le N: 7\notin n\}$. Prove $S_N[A_N]$ has a Hamiltonian path for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Hat centres and bounded displacement
words: Same question for the hat: can the tile centres be matched to a square grid by moving each point a bounded distance?
math: Decide whether the centre set of a hat tiling is bounded-displacement equivalent to a lattice of the same density.

title: Square-sum chains in primes
words: Show there are arbitrarily long chains of primes where neighbours sum to squares.
math: Prove for every $k$ there are primes $p_1,\dots,p_k$ with $p_i+p_{i+1}$ a perfect square for all $i<k$.

title: Entering the 4p+1 loop
words: Show a typical prime enters the 4p + 1 map's eight-prime loop in about log log p steps.
math: For $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$, prove that the number of steps to enter the 8-cycle is $\sim c\log\log p$ for all but $o(\pi(x))$ primes $p\le x$, and find $c$.

title: The square-sum avoidance game
words: Players take turns choosing unused numbers from 1 to N. Whoever picks a number summing to a square with any already-chosen number loses. Decide the winner for all large N.
math: Determine the outcome class of the avoidance game on $S_N$ (normal play, a move creating an $S_N$-edge inside the chosen set loses) for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Hat tilings of convex regions
words: Show no convex polygon can be tiled exactly by hats.
math: Prove no convex polygon is a finite union of interior-disjoint congruent hats (reflections allowed), or exhibit one.

title: Midpoint-prime map hitting primes
words: Show the midpoint-prime orbit of almost every start passes through a prime at least once.
math: Prove $\{n: \exists k,\ m^k(n)\text{ prime}\}$ has natural density 1.

title: The 7p+4 dozen
words: Under p ↦ largest prime factor of 7p + 4, every tested prime ends in one loop of length 12. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(7p+4)$ on primes enters a single cycle of length 12, and identify it.

title: Counting square-sum chains
words: Count the ways to line up 1 to N with neighbours summing to squares. Find the leading growth.
math: Let $h(N)$ be the number of Hamiltonian paths of $S_N$. Prove $\log h(N)=(\tfrac12+o(1))N\log N$.

title: The 4p+1 funnel
words: Map a prime p to the largest prime factor of 4p + 1. Every prime tested falls into one loop of eight primes. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$ on primes enters the cycle $5\to7\to29\to13\to53\to71\to19\to11\to5$.

title: Snort on square sums
words: Two players colour numbers up to N, one red and one blue. Neither may colour a number summing to a square with one of the opponent's colour. The player who cannot move loses. Decide who wins for large N.
math: Determine the outcome of the partizan game Snort on $S_N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Largest factor of consecutive-prime products
words: Show that p_n·p_(n+1) + 1 has a prime factor much bigger than p_(n+1), infinitely often.
math: Prove $P(p_np_{n+1}+1)>p_{n+1}^{1.5}$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: Prime-power Collatz in every odd base
words: Replace 3n + 1 by an + 1 for any odd a and divide by its largest prime-power factor. Prove every orbit reaches 1, for every a.
math: For odd $a\ge3$ let $c_a(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even), $(an+1)/q(an+1)$ ($n$ odd), $q(m)$ the largest prime power dividing $m$. Prove every orbit of every $c_a$ reaches $1$.

title: Square-plus-one collisions
words: Count pairs n ≠ m up to x for which n² + 1 and m² + 1 have the same largest prime factor.
math: Find the asymptotic number of pairs $n<m\le x$ with $P(n^2+1)=P(m^2+1)$.

title: Prime-sum perfect matchings
words: Pair each odd number up to 2n with an even one so every pair sums to a prime. Count the pairings, to leading order.
math: Prove the number of perfect matchings of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ equals $\big(\frac{n}{e\log n}\big)^{n(1+o(1))}$.

title: Rational fibres of the Alpöge map
words: The 2026 Jacobian counterexample sends three rational points to one point. Show infinitely many rational target points have three rational preimages.
math: For Alpöge's Keller map $F:\mathbb{Q}^3\to\mathbb{Q}^3$, prove $\{y\in\mathbb{Q}^3:|F^{-1}(y)\cap\mathbb{Q}^3|=3\}$ is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{A}^3$.

title: Blow-up near a wall
words: Show the 2026 forced blow-up mechanism also works in a half-space with no-slip wall, with the singularity on the wall.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ such that Navier–Stokes in $\mathbb{R}^3_+$ with no-slip, from rest, blows up in finite time at a boundary point.

title: Prime Nim on two piles with a shared move
words: In two-pile Prime Nim you may also take the same prime from both piles. Show losing positions lie near a line of irrational slope.
math: For moves $(a,b)\to(a-p,b),(a,b-p),(a-p,b-p)$, $p$ prime, prove the P-positions $(a_k,b_k)$, $a_k<b_k$, satisfy $b_k/a_k\to\phi$ for some $\phi$, and show $\phi\notin\mathbb{Q}$.

title: Prime Nim parity bias
words: Show Prime Nim losing positions are equally often odd and even.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x: G(n)=0,\ n\ \text{odd}\}\sim\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0,\ n\ \text{even}\}$.

title: Prime-sum graph is an expander
words: The prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n is bipartite. Show its second-largest eigenvalue is a fixed fraction below the largest.
math: Prove $\lambda_2\le(1-c)\lambda_1$ for the adjacency matrix of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$, for an absolute $c>0$ and all large $n$.

title: Spectre-tiled squares
words: Decide whether a square can be cut exactly into finitely many spectres.
math: Decide whether some square in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a finite union of interior-disjoint congruent copies of the (straight-edged) Tile(1,1).
